I am a PhD student in Political Science at [American University](https://www.american.edu/spa/gov/) in Washington, DC, specializing in political methodology and comparative politics. My research sits at the intersection of **comparative politics, political economy, and data science**, with a focus on the politics of energy and climate — how infrastructure failures, energy transitions, and new energy demands shape electoral behavior and regulatory accountability.

Before my PhD, I completed a dual M.A. in European Studies at Palacký University and Uppsala University, and I bring several years of experience in quantitative research, statistical modeling in R, GIS, and policy-facing writing.
